title: Cotangent sheaf model and its standard functoriality comparison
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $\mathcal C_{B/A}$ be the opposite category of polynomial $A$-algebras $P$ equipped with an $A$-algebra map $P\to B$, whose morphisms before taking opposites are $A$-algebra maps commuting with augmentations. Use a common infinite variable-cardinality bound containing all rings involved and a small skeleton in [def-weil-size-convention], with identity-cover topology. Let $\mathcal O(P\to B)=P$, with augmentation $\mathcal O\to\underline B$, and define the $\underline B$-module presheaf $F_{B/A}(P\to B)=\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P B$ with restriction maps induced by algebra maps and universal differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\pi:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_{B/A}),\underline B)\to(*,B)$ and its derived lower shriek be as in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\theta_{B/A}:L\pi_!F_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{B/A}$$
in $D(B)$, where $L_{B/A}$ is the standard simplicial cotangent complex of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. More generally, for every module presheaf $F$ and every polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ in that node, $L\pi_!F$ is canonically identified with the alternating differential complex $s(F(P_\bullet\to B))$, naturally in $F$ and in morphisms of augmented resolutions. On $F_{B/A}$ this agrees with that node's comparison isomorphism for polynomial resolutions.
For an arbitrary commutative square $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, define $u:\mathcal C_{B/A}\to\mathcal C_{B'/A'}$ by $(P\to B)\mapsto(P\otimes_A A'\to B')$ and let $t:F_{B/A}\to u^{-1}F_{B'/A'}$ be the $b$-semilinear transformation
$$\mathrm dp\otimes r\longmapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes b(r).$$
If $T=L\pi_!(u,t)$ is the map represented by the bar-chain formula of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], then
$$\theta_{B'/A'}\,T=f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}\,\theta_{B/A}$$
after restriction of scalars to $B$, where $f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}$ is the canonical map induced by standard resolutions in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. The identity is for all ring squares, without any injectivity or flatness assumption on $a$ or $b$.

source.place: Tags 08PS (lemma-identify-pi-shriek), 08PT (lemma-pi-shriek-standard), 08PU (lemma-compute-cotangent-complex), 08QI (remark-resolution), 08QL (section-functoriality), including the omitted agreement of sheaf and standard-resolution maps, isolated here as a supporting comparison lemma.

proof.text: Take universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ with $A,B$ and the resolutions $\mathcal U$-small; the skeleton $\mathcal D=\mathcal C_{B/A}^{op}$ is a small full subcategory of $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ of [lem-trf-polynomial-presentation-homology]. A polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] (the standard one is such by that node) has polynomial terms surjecting onto $B$ and $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ a quasi-isomorphism, so its underlying augmentation is a trivial Kan fibration by [lem-trf-polynomial-augmentation-boundary]; transport its terms into $\mathcal D$. Clause (1) of [lem-trf-polynomial-resolution-universal-evaluation] with $R=B$ gives $\alpha_{P,F}=j_F^{-1}a_{P,F}:s(F(P_\bullet))\simeq L\pi_!F$, natural in $F$ and in augmented resolution maps, with the bar sign $(-1)^{n(n+1)/2}$ fixed. Inverting it proves the general resolution formula.

The rules $\mathrm dp\otimes r\mapsto\mathrm d(w(p))\otimes r$ respect additivity, Leibniz and $\mathrm d(A)=0$ of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the tensor balancing, as $w$ commutes with the augmentations; identity and composition hold on generators. So $F_{B/A}=\mathcal F_{B/A}\circ i$ for $\mathcal F_{B/A}(T)=\Omega_{T/A}\otimes_TB$ on $\mathcal D_{B/A}$, and $s(F_{B/A}(P^{\mathrm{std}}))=L_{B/A}$. The comparison of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] is $c_P=(a^{\mathrm{big}}_{\mathrm{std}})^{-1}a^{\mathrm{big}}_P$, from [lem-trf-polynomial-presentation-homology] for $R=B$ and $\mathcal F_{B/A}$. Clause (2) of [lem-trf-polynomial-resolution-universal-evaluation] gives $c_P=\alpha_{\mathrm{std}}^{-1}\alpha_P$. Put $\theta_{B/A}=\alpha_{\mathrm{std},F_{B/A}}^{-1}$; then $\theta_{B/A}\alpha_P=c_P$ for every polynomial resolution, with no arbitrary choice.

For a ring square, [lem-trf-polynomial-square-bar-naturality] gives $v:T\mapsto(T\otimes_AA'\to B')$, the transformation $t$ of the statement, the standard semilinear map $h:P^{\mathrm{std}}\to P'^{\mathrm{std}}$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] and $k:vP^{\mathrm{std}}\to P'^{\mathrm{std}}$, $k(p\otimes a')=h(p)a'$. Since $F'(k_n)t(\mathrm dp\otimes r)=\mathrm d(h_n(p))\otimes b(r)$, $s(F'(k)t)$ is the map $f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}$ of the coherence node. Transport isomorphisms into the skeleton are absorbed in $t$ and $k$; by [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] they do not change $T$. Clause (3) of [lem-trf-polynomial-resolution-universal-evaluation] ($\rho=b$, $G=F'$) gives $\alpha_{\mathrm{std}'}f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}=T\alpha_{\mathrm{std}}$ after restriction to $B$. Composing with $\alpha_{\mathrm{std}'}^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{std}}^{-1}$ gives $\theta_{B'/A'}T=f^{\mathrm{std}}_{a,b}\theta_{B/A}$. Only the endpoints are resolutions, so every square (e.g. non-flat $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf F_2$) is covered.
